speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me exactly how long it has been there and if you noticed any preceding injury or rash? Additionally, have you had any recent fevers, weight loss, or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasculitis (specifically Erythema Elevatum Diabeticum or Pyoderma Gangrenosum, given the history of diabetes, Crohn's, and ant bite trigger).

Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the ulcerative nature of the lesion, I need to rule out infection and assess the lesion's depth. Please describe the appearance of the wound bed (punched-out with undermined edges vs. flat base), and have you noticed any joint pain or mouth sores recently? REQUEST TEST: WBC count and ESR; REQUEST TEST: Tissue biopsy for histopathology and culture.
